name: Clash Royale — Double Elixir & Overtime Sudden Death
one_line: Real-time card/tower hybrid where the last 60s of a match doubles resource regen and adds a first-hit-wins overtime, with 3x elixir in the final overtime minute
take_what: Elixir regen rate literally doubles (2.8s/pt -> 1.4s/pt) for the final third of the match, then triples in overtime; over 40% of matches are decided in this compressed window because both players can suddenly afford aggressive plays they were saving up for
constraint: none - pure numeric mechanism, not IP-bound

name: Risk of Rain 2 — Director Coefficient Difficulty Scaling
one_line: Roguelike horde-survival where a global 'coeff' rises with playtime and jumps 15% at every stage-clear, governing what the spawn Director can afford to send at you
take_what: coeff = (playerFactor + minutes*timeFactor) * 1.15^stagesCompleted — a single exponential-ish scalar that both (a) increases enemy budget over time and (b) forces the spawner to stop sending cheap/lone enemies once coeff is high, guaranteeing spawns never trivially decay into nothing
constraint: none - formula shape only, not code

name: Plants vs. Zombies — Flag Zombie Huge Waves
one_line: Lane-defense game whose on-screen progress bar telegraphs periodic 'huge wave' spikes led by a Flag Zombie, roughly every 10th wave, visible to the player in advance
take_what: A visible, always-on progress meter that spikes with a distinct marker (flag icon) BEFORE the huge wave hits, so the player can see the coming crunch and choose to spend resources/set up defense in advance rather than being surprised

name: Bloons TD 6 — Round Escalation and MOAB-class Spike Rounds
one_line: Tower defense where round difficulty escalates from single weak bloons (round 1) to camo/lead/regrow MOAB-class bosses by round 40, with named spike rounds forcing tower repositioning
take_what: Escalation isn't smooth — specific 'spike rounds' introduce a wholly new threat property (camo, lead, regrow) that invalidates the player's current setup and forces an active response, not just 'bigger numbers'

name: They Are Billions — Day/Night Swarm Cycle
one_line: City-builder/tower-defense hybrid alternating calm build-up phases with periodic zombie swarm attacks, culminating in one final overwhelming swarm from all map edges
take_what: Structural rhythm of build-phase -> attack-phase -> build-phase, with each attack phase strictly larger than the last and the final attack an explicit 'everything at once' climax rather than a continuation of gradual scaling

name: Defender's Quest — Optimizing Tower Defense for Focus and Thinking (Lars Doucet)
one_line: Design essay arguing tower defense should reward strategic THINKING over twitch reflexes via total time control (pause + variable speed) and total information (full stat readouts, wave preview)
take_what: Resource/cooldown costs are the only thing stopping pause-and-plan from being degenerate — action economy, not reaction speed, is what makes placement decisions feel weighty; pairs with full pre-battle visibility of what enemies/waves are coming so choices are informed, not blind

name: Risk of Rain 2 General Discussion — 'Does difficulty keep scaling after HAHAHAHA' thread
one_line: Player thread on the felt experience of RoR2's unbounded difficulty scaling and where it stops feeling fair vs starts feeling like an inevitable timer-driven loss
take_what: Players explicitly describe unbounded escalation without a visible cap or endgame as eventually feeling like 'the clock is the real enemy, not the monsters' — a caution that Limen's turn-based escalation needs a legible ceiling or resolution point, not infinite ramp
constraint: none - anecdotal, treat as directional signal not hard data

name: Kingdom Rush — Wave-based Tower Defense Series
one_line: Classic wave-based tower defense with a manual 'call next wave early' button that lets skilled players compress downtime and stack overlapping waves for bonus rewards
take_what: Giving the player agency to voluntarily overlap/accelerate the next escalation step (rather than a fixed timer) rewards mastery and creates player-driven tempo instead of only designer-driven tempo
